title: で — where it happens, and how
pattern: place で verb / means で verb
explanation: で marks where an action happens: {家|いえ}で{晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べます — I have dinner at home. It also marks how, or with what: {電車|でんしゃ}で{行|い}きます — I go by train; {日本語|にほんご}で{話|はな}しましょう — let’s talk in Japanese.
natural: The everyday way to say by train, by car, in English, with chopsticks: お{箸|はし}で{食|た}べる.
stiff: Where someone simply is takes に: {家|いえ}にいます. Where something is done takes で: {家|いえ}で{働|はたら}きます. Mixing the two up is the most common particle slip.

examples.japanese: 家で晩ご飯を食べます。
examples.furigana: {家|いえ}で{晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べます。

gap.after: {晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べます。
gap.why: Eating is something you do there: で.

examples.japanese: 電車で会社に行きます。
examples.furigana: {電車|でんしゃ}で{会社|かいしゃ}に{行|い}きます。
examples.english: I go to work by train.

gap.after: {会社|かいしゃ}に{行|い}きます。
gap.why: How you go: by train, 電車で.

examples.japanese: 今日は日本語で話そう。
examples.furigana: {今日|きょう}は{日本語|にほんご}で{話|はな}そう。

gap.before: {今日|きょう}は{日本語|にほんご}
gap.why: In a language: 日本語で.

examples.japanese: 駅の前で待っています。
examples.furigana: {駅|えき}の{前|まえ}で{待|ま}っています。
examples.romaji: eki no mae de matte imasu
examples.english: I’ll be waiting in front of the station.

gap.why: Waiting is something you do there, so where takes で.
